selected.name: fips2go 0.6.0
selected.summary: The release adds human-readable Nostr identity labels to FIPS mesh nodes. That changes an operator-facing addressing workflow and makes the mesh mechanics useful to explain.

selected.name: fips-initramfs 0.1.0
selected.summary: The first release enables remote LUKS unlock through an npub-addressed FIPS mesh during early boot. Its verified September 6 publication is outside the automatic reporting window, so it is retained only by the authenticated mandatory catch-up override and does not establish a scoring precedent.

selected.name: Grain 0.8.0-rc4
selected.summary: The release turns relay health data into an operator dashboard rather than exposing only raw status. It gives relay operators a concrete reliability workflow and a useful explanation of health signals.

selected.name: Marmot Protocol 0.10.4
selected.summary: The release makes local sends durable across process interruption. It materially changes encrypted group-message reliability and exposes a persistence design worth explaining.

selected.name: MintRadar
selected.summary: In-window work adds NIP-87 announcement persistence, NUT-06 same-operator detection, shareable comparison state, and Nostr naddr links. Those changes make Cashu mint comparison more accountable and connect its state directly to Nostr identities.

selected.name: Nostr WoT Oracle 0.3.1
selected.summary: The release makes follow and mute graph ingestion restart-safe and revision-bound. That is a concrete reliability change for services answering Nostr trust queries.

selected.name: Nostr WoT SDK 1.0.2
selected.summary: The release compresses browser-side social-graph storage while preserving trust queries. It changes the practical cost of client-side WoT features and offers a clear storage tradeoff.

selected.name: napplet.soy
selected.summary: The project publishes small sandboxed Nostr programs with a current tagged runtime. It provides a concrete distribution and execution model for app handlers rather than another generic web client.

selected.name: RelayKit
selected.summary: RelayKit now packages a self-hosted Nostr stack behind a one-command installation path. This is a material direction change from the relay-discovery client Compass covered in April and has direct operator value.

selected.name: Threshold Sessions
selected.summary: The NIP-34 repository documents a working path for normalizing, redacting, encrypting, and publishing coding-session datasets. It makes privacy-preserving training-data exchange over Nostr technically reviewable.

selected.name: White Noise Android 2026.9.21
selected.summary: The September 21 Android release improves private Marmot chat delivery and voice tools, and adds shareable profile and invite QR cards. The GitHub release supplies primary evidence beyond the Zapstore listing that the earlier triage skipped.

selected.name: Nostr Mail Client 0.16.0
selected.summary: The release adds per-recipient delivery choices to a Nostr mail client. Users gain direct control over how each recipient is reached, making the update more than routine maintenance.

selected.name: Amber 6.6.5
selected.summary: The Android signer separates backup encryption from application permissions. That sharpens the security boundary for key backup and delegated signing.

selected.name: Amethyst 1.16.0
selected.summary: The release fixes the single-flight authorization guarantee for fast Blossom signers. That is a concrete signer-boundary correction documented in the cited release rather than post-release feature work.

selected.name: Alby Extension 3.15.0
selected.summary: The extension hardens website-initiated Nostr and wallet requests. The security boundary is user-visible and useful to explain to web integrators.

selected.name: LaWallet NWC 2.7.1
selected.summary: The release unifies zap receipt handling across wallet interactions. That changes observable NWC interoperability rather than only internal implementation.

selected.name: NoorNote 1.6.1
selected.summary: The release adds a configurable Addons overview and fixes broken naddr and npub rendering inside URLs. Those changes provide a visible extension-management surface and safer Nostr identifier handling without misattributing the 1.6.0 calendar feature.

selected.name: Citrine 3.2.0
selected.summary: The local relay bounds aggregator memory in a released Android build. That is an operator-visible reliability improvement for continuous local event ingestion.

selected.name: Wisp 1.2.4
selected.summary: The Android client routes thread and notification reads strictly through inbox relays and adds NIP-22 comment handling. Those released changes alter delivery behavior and interoperability; 1.2.5 is excluded because it is only a version bump.

selected.name: nostr-wot-extension 0.8.0
selected.summary: The browser extension restores opt-in graph queries in a tagged release. It gives users a bounded trust-query capability with an explicit consent surface.

selected.name: pakstr 0.21.0–0.24.0
selected.summary: The release series adds Android NIP-46 bunker lifecycle hardening and NIP-98 proxying, followed by NIP-55 signing and persistent runtime configuration. The 0.24.0 icon-only change is not presented as the milestone.

selected.name: Nail 0.2.2
selected.summary: The Nostr email bridge makes attachment failures non-fatal. That fixes a real delivery workflow and has a clear interoperability consequence.

selected.name: Mostro CLI 0.16.2
selected.summary: The release removes its legacy chat transport. The resulting protocol path is simpler and changes how the client communicates with Mostro services.

selected.name: Dart NDK 0.10.0-dev.4–dev.5
selected.summary: The dev.4 release adds NIP-82 application-update support, while dev.5 hardens relay delivery and Cashu quote handling. Treating the pair as one in-window series keeps the application-update claim bound to the release that actually introduced it.

selected.name: BitBlik 0.11.0
selected.summary: The release brings dispute handling into the application. It exposes a substantive marketplace workflow rather than a cosmetic update.

selected.name: NIP-02 petnames
selected.summary: The merged change clarifies how follow-list petnames should be interpreted. It affects an interoperable kind-3 field and removes ambiguity for client implementers.

selected.name: NIP-86 relay management methods
selected.summary: The proposal adds clear and list methods to the relay management API. Operators and tooling gain explicit administrative capabilities with observable relay effects.

selected.name: NIP-69 stable order creation time
selected.summary: The proposal gives trading orders a stable creation-time rule. That affects ordering and replacement semantics across marketplace implementations.

selected.name: NIP-A3 payment-address proofs
selected.summary: The proposal defines proof of ownership for payment addresses. It connects Nostr identities to payment endpoints with direct verification consequences.

selected.name: BUD-16 directory manifests
selected.summary: The proposal defines deterministic directory manifests for Blossom storage. It makes directory state portable and verifiable across servers.

selected.name: Marmot encrypted group polls
selected.summary: The merged work adds polls to encrypted Marmot groups. It introduces new group-event behavior with direct client interoperability implications.

selected.name: Marmot reports and admin deletion
selected.summary: The merged work combines group reports with administrative deletion. It changes moderation authority and event-handling behavior in encrypted groups.

selected.name: NWC-13 connection budgets
selected.summary: The proposal lets clients query connection budgets. That gives wallet integrations a concrete resource-management signal and a useful interoperability contract.

selected.name: NIP-30 custom emoji
selected.summary: NIP-30 defines shortcode-to-image mappings for custom emoji in event content and profiles. It has not been a prior Compass deep dive, and current implementations in Amethyst, Wisp, and Nostria make creation and rendering behavior directly testable.

selected.name: NIP-71 video events
selected.summary: NIP-71 defines addressable and regular video events plus media metadata needed for playback and discovery. It has not been a prior Compass deep dive, and current implementations in Amethyst, Wisp, and Resonote provide three independent code paths.
